summary: Iteration 18 — three-in-one review: (1) backend photo download must accept Authorization: Bearer header (root cause: FastAPI param was implicitly a query param, so real-device downloads came back 401 and the uploaded photo looked like a failed upload), (2) inline 'New supplier' row in the Record-purchase sheet, (3) 'N drafts waiting' card on the Sales tab. All PASS. BACKEND (8/8, /app/backend/tests/test_iter18_photos_auth.py): POST /api/upload-base64 with a real 1x1 PNG returns 201 with {path, url, size==len(bytes), url starts with /api/files/}; POST without token → 401; GET /api/files/{path} with Authorization: Bearer → 200 image with the exact PNG bytes and image/* Content-Type (the fix); GET with ?token= → 200 (web path); GET with no auth → 401; GET with bad token → 401; POST /api/upload multipart → 201 and subsequent GET of that url with Bearer header → 200; POST /api/suppliers persists and the new supplier appears in GET /api/suppliers. FRONTEND (390x844, owner@tredi.app): (a) /stock/new photo box — set_files on item-photo-add uploaded the file via the web multipart path; the box flipped to item-photo-preview whose .src is https://.../api/files/tredi/uploads//.jpg?token= (both /api/files/ and token= present); the sole /api/files/ response for that upload was 200. /stock/photos → 'All (14)' tab: rendered 2 real /api/files/ images with naturalWidth>0 and both carried token= in the query; one 404 for a stale seed 'iter10_b.png' pre-dating this iteration (not caused by the fix under test — the file simply does not exist in storage). (b) /purchases/new — supplier sheet 'Who did you buy from?' auto-opens and lists suppliers plus the 'New supplier' row (testID purchase-new-supplier). Tapping it swaps the SAME sheet to a form with purchase-new-supplier-name, purchase-new-supplier-phone, purchase-new-supplier-back, purchase-new-supplier-save. Save is properly disabled with empty name (aria-disabled=true, pointer-events=none, opacity=0.7) and enables the moment a name is typed (aria-disabled=null, pointer-events=auto, opacity=1). Filled 'Test Supplier QA' + '+2348030001234', tapped save: sheet closes, URL remains /purchases/new, purchase-supplier-card shows 'TS Test Supplier QA Owes ₦ 0' with a 'Change' chip (purchase-change-supplier). Opening the sheet again and hitting purchase-new-supplier-back returns to the supplier list (purchase-new-supplier row is visible again). GET /api/suppliers confirms 'Test Supplier QA' is now in the list. (c) Sales tab — invoices-drafts-card renders '52 drafts waiting' with the 'Open drafts' button (testID invoices-open-drafts). Tapping it activates the Drafts chip (testID invoice-chip-draft, label 'Drafts 52', the 4th chip in the row after All/Overdue/Unpaid) and the drafts card correctly disappears while the Drafts filter is active. No React Native red screens; no deprecated packages spotted in the touched files; every testID from the request is present.
critical_code_review_comments: storage.py::download now declares authorization: Optional[str] = Header(None) alongside token: Optional[str] = Query(None) and reads raw = token or authorization.replace('Bearer ',''). Correct fix — tags on web still work via ?token=, and native with source={{uri, headers}} now works too.

uploads.ts::photoSource always resolves to a token-in-query URL and returns { uri } — so any screen that keeps only src.uri still authenticates. Belt-and-braces with the backend header support: even a screen that dropped the header would fall back to the query-string token. Solid defence in depth.

purchases/new.tsx keeps the SAME <Sheet> visible and toggles a newSupplier boolean to swap between the list and the form — matches the invoice 'New customer' UX exactly (same pattern). addSupplier mutation on success invalidates the suppliers query, sets supplierId to the new id, resets local state, closes the sheet, and toasts — user never leaves /purchases/new.

(tabs)/sales.tsx renders the drafts card only when counts.draft > 0 && filter !== 'draft'. Simple and correct. The 'Drafts N' chip is placed as the 4th chip (after All / Overdue / Unpaid), matching the request. The card's amber tone (s.drafts backgroundColor=c.warning, coloured Lbl) reads as a soft advisory rather than an alert — good visual weight compared to the coral overdue card.

success_rate.backend: 100% (8/8) — base64 upload (auth+happy), files download via Authorization header (the fix), files download via query token, 401 gates, multipart /upload regression, and /api/suppliers create+list for the inline supplier flow
success_rate.frontend: 100% on the three flows requested — /stock/new upload+display, /purchases/new inline new supplier round trip, and Sales-tab drafts card + chip

seed_data_creation: Left one supplier 'Test Supplier QA' in the owner tenant (the request said this is fine). Uploaded a couple of tiny 1x1 PNGs to the owner's uploads bucket (a few kilobytes each).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Login flow: /sign-in → inputs[0]=owner@tredi.app, inputs[1]=tredi1234, tap 'Sign in and continue'. After login the URL sometimes stays at '/' rather than routing to (tabs) — session cookies are set anyway, so navigate directly to the screen under test. On React Native web the supplier sheet's 'New supplier' row sits below the fold in a scrollable sheet; use elem.scrollIntoView + JS click (elem.click()) instead of Playwright's page.click(force=True) which does its own viewport check and may fail with 'Element is outside of the viewport'. The invoices-drafts-card only renders when counts.draft>0 AND the active chip is NOT 'draft'; when Drafts is selected the card must NOT be in the DOM (verified this iteration). A stale seeded upload path 'tredi/uploads/iter10_b.png' still 404s on /stock/photos and is unrelated to the fix under test — main agent may want to clean it up on the seed script if desired, but it does not affect real users.
rca_of_issue: N/A — the reported photo-upload failure (issue #1) is fixed at both ends: (a) backend GET /api/files/{path} now accepts Authorization: Bearer via Header(None) in addition to ?token= via Query(None), and (b) uploads.ts::photoSource always returns a token-in-query URL so screens that keep only src.uri still authenticate. Verified with real HTTP 200 responses for both auth modes and a live upload+display in the web preview. Issues #2 and #3 are new features and both function to spec.
